items.text: Ask for the exact rule in writing: which semester you join, which subjects you skip, and whether the final degree certificate says anything different from a regular 2-year MBA graduate's certificate.
A verbal promise from a counsellor is not a policy.

blocks.heading: Mistakes People Make with This Route

items.text: Engineering lateral entry (diploma to BTech year 2) is a nationally standardised, AICTE-governed scheme.
A UGC RTI response has confirmed that MBA is treated as a 2-year course under UGC guidance, and regulators have separately warned against fake, unrecognised 1-year or "10-day" MBA advertisements.
Education marketplaces and individual colleges have a financial incentive to make lateral entry sound simple and universally available.
Do not decide this from a college's marketing page alone, and do not assume the term means what the much more common BTech lateral-entry route means.

If a genuine lateral-entry MBA fits your situation, verify the institute's UGC/AICTE standing for that exact program, get the equivalence claim in writing, and compare the real time saved against the recognition risk before you commit.

If the honest answer is that you do not have a firm, specific reason to rush, a well-placed regular 2-year MBA or a genuine Executive MBA usually protects your income and career options better than a faster but less verified route, the goal is a stronger, high-income skill portfolio and earlier financial freedom, not just a shorter timetable.

items.text: Prior PG study route: you completed year 1 of a PGDM, a relevant Master's degree, or an equivalent postgraduate management program at another recognised institute, and are transferring that credit into a new institute's year 2.

blocks.heading: Red Flags to Check Before You Pay

items.text: Is the university itself currently listed as UGC-recognised, with an active, verifiable status for the current academic year.
Is the specific MBA/PGDM program AICTE-approved (where AICTE approval applies), not just the university in general.

Does the final degree certificate read identically to the institute's standard 2-year MBA, with no separate lateral-entry notation that could raise questions later with an employer, a government recruiter, or a doctoral admissions committee.
